key_insight: Micropillar compression reveals that in anorthite, mechanical twinning is easier to activate than slip, and slip strength drops strongly with temperature while twinning CRSS stays near 300 MPa.
engineering_relevance: These results help constrain crystal-plastic constitutive models for plagioclase-rich crustal rocks, improving predictions of deformation, anisotropy, and rheology under geologic conditions.
method: Focused-ion-beam milled ~1 µm micropillars from three crystal orientations of an anorthite single crystal.
Compressed 36 pillars inside an SEM at 25, 300, and 800 °C.
Used constant displacement-rate loading to infer CRSS and compare twinning vs. slip activation.
evidence_signal: The study reports orientation-dependent pillar deformation data showing ~300 MPa CRSS for pericline twinning, temperature-insensitive twinning, and a strong temperature dependence of yield stress for slip-active pillars.
watch_item: Micropillar tests probe highly localized deformation in small volumes, so extrapolating directly to bulk crustal behavior should account for size effects and crystal-orientation sensitivity.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
